criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
criteria.evidence: Purdue GIS FID 290 identifies BELL / Bell Tower at 325 Centennial Mall Drive. I projected the 4-vertex source envelope with the documented local conversion; the convex hull of actual base-foot vertices has a sampled symmetric boundary discrepancy of 0.027 m (sampling interval 0.05 m).

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
criteria.evidence: GIS polygon area centroid and manifest placement differ by 0.000002 m. Oriented-envelope edge angle differs by 0.000° modulo 90°, and sorted envelope dimension errors are 0.031 m and 0.034 m. The model uses the manifest local frame; the master placement instance itself was not opened.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof
criteria.evidence: Purdue News states 160 ft and four historic bells; the actual evaluated model height is 48.767998 m versus 48.768 m, an error of 0.000002 m. Official Purdue photos show the pyramidal metal roof and open belfry. GIS reports one level; a freestanding tower has no normal occupied-floor stack to infer.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
criteria.evidence: Reopened/rendered geometry includes red-brick shaft, limestone base arches/string courses, four clock dials, four historic bells, four open belfry arches, and pyramidal roof. The official Purdue photos corroborate these signature features; the plaque text and subordinate architectural dimensions are explicitly representative/estimated.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and evidence completeness
criteria.evidence: Scene `Building_bell_tower`, collection `Asset_bell_tower`, 578 manifest-matched objects; collection-only export reopened with the same objects and no camera/lights. No unpacked textures or linked libraries. Detailed source evidence and build script are present under `modular/bell_tower_work/`; canonical `modular/buildings/build_bell_tower.py` is absent.

source_limitations: GIS polygon is a map envelope, not certified structural survey.
Published source supports overall height but not a measured set of subordinate elevations.
The exact plaque text, plaque seal, and internal mechanism are not verified.
The master placement instance was not opened.

findings: The model aligns its structural base envelope and placement to official Purdue GIS within centimeter-scale tolerances.
Published 160 ft height matches evaluated geometry to under 0.001 mm; official sources support red brick, limestone trim, four bells, and the clock/tower identity.
The exported collection is portable and reopens with the expected manifest contract.

Remaining evidence gap: the dedicated build module is stored at modular/bell_tower_work/build_tower.py rather than modular/buildings/build_bell_tower.py; the master placement marker was not independently inspected.
Fine dimensions and plaque inscription remain estimates or representative rather than surveyed/facsimile detail.
